verses.1: And Gilad was a powerful man. He was the son of a beautiful woman. Gilad gave birth to Yiftah.
verses.2: And Gilead’s wife gave birth to sons for him. These sons grew up, and they drove out Jephte. They said to him, “Do not live in our father’s house, for you are the son of another woman.”
verses.3: And Yiftah ran away from his brothers. He settled in a good land. Then people who were evil came to Yiftah and joined him.
verses.4: And from those days onward, the children of Israel fought against the Canaanites.
verses.5: And when the people of Gilad fought against Israel, the elders of Gilad went to take Yiftah from the land of Good.
verses.6: And they said, “Let us open the gates and you will become our commanders. Then we will fight against the children of Ammon.”
verses.7: And He said to the elders of Gilgal, “Don’t you hate me? Why did you drive me out of my father’s house? And why have you come to me now, when it becomes difficult for you?”
verses.8: And the elders of Gilgal said to Yiftah, “Now let us return. Come with us, and we will fight against the children of Ammon. You will become our leader over all the people of Gilgal.”
verses.9: And Yiftah said to the elders of Gilgal, “Will you let me fight against the children of Ammon again? Then Jehovah will give them into my hands. I will be your leader.”
verses.10: And the elders of Gilgal said to Jephthah, “May the LORD listen to our prayers. If not, then it will not be done according to your words.”
verses.11: And Yiftah went with the elders of Gilgal. The people placed him above them, as their leader. Yiftah spoke all his words before Jehovah at the temple.
verses.12: And Yiftah sent his soldiers to the king of Beni’Amon, saying, “What do you want? Why have you come to me to fight in my land?”
verses.13: And the king of Beni-Ammon said to the officials of Jiphthah: “Israel has taken my land from me, taking away my women from Egypt, from Arnon to Hebron and from Yarden. Now, let them be returned to their homes in peace.”
verses.14: And Yiftah also gathered his men and sent them to the king of Beni’Amun.
verses.15: And he said to him, “Yephetah shall not take the land of Moab and the land of the children of Ammon.”
verses.16: For their mothers were from Egypt. Israel went through the desert until it reached the Sea of Galilee. Then they arrived at Kadesh.
verses.17: And Israel sent servants to King Adonai, saying, “Please allow us to live in your land.” But King Adonai did not listen to them. Then they sent messengers to King Moab, but he also did not listen to them. In the end, Israel remained in Kadesh.
verses.18: And he went into the desert, and he conquered the land of Edom and the land of Moab. He came from the east towards the land of Moab. They stopped by Arnon’s river, but they did not enter Moab’s territory, because Arnon’s river was part of Moab’s territory.
verses.19: And Israel sent servants to Sihon, king of the Amorites, in Heshbon. Israel said to him, “Please allow me to pass through your land until I reach my place.”
verses.20: And Sihon did not believe Israel. He crossed the Jordan River. Sihon gathered all his people together and camped at Jahaz. Then he fought against Israel.
verses.21: And Jehovah, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into the hands of Israel. Israel conquered all the land of the Amorites, and they became the rulers of that land.
verses.22: And they inherited all the borders of the Amorites, from Arnon to Jabok, from the desert to the Jordan.
verses.23: And now, LORD, God of Israel, remove those Amorites from before Your people Israel. And You shall inherit them.
verses.24: Do not take what your ruler gives you as if it were from your God. Instead, give back to Him everything that the Lord our God has given us.
verses.25: And now, may you be good to those who are like Benjamin’s sons, the kings of Moab. They have a great deal in common with Israel. If we fight against them, then let us do so.
verses.26: In the days of Israel, in its cities and towns, and in all the places that were built by Aarón over the course of three hundred years… It’s unknown why they weren’t saved at that time.
verses.27: And I have not sinned against you. Yet you do evil to me by fighting against me. Jehovah will judge today between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.
verses.28: And the king of Benjamin heard nothing of what Yiftah had said, who had been sent to him.
verses.29: And a wind from Jehovah blew over Gilgal and Manasseh. It also blew over Mizpah of Gilgal. And from Mizpah of Gilgal, it blew over the children of Judah.
verses.30: And Jephthah swore by Jehovah, and said, “If you give me back my people’s children, then I will give them back to you.”
verses.31: And he who comes out from the doors of my house, when I call to him again, will be peaceful among the children of Ammon. He will become a servant of Jehovah, and Jehovah will raise him up.
verses.32: And Yiftah went to the children of Amun to fight against them. But Jehovah handed them over into his hands.
verses.33: And he conquered from one city to another. Until you arrived, he gave him forty cities. And even beyond that, he destroyed a great number of vineyards. Then the children of Ammon submitted to the children of Israel.
verses.34: And Yiftah entered his house. There, he saw that his daughter was coming to call him, with complaints and worries on her face. She was the only one who could help him; he had no other children or daughters to rely on.
verses.35: And when he saw her, he tore his clothes. He said, “Oh daughter of mine! You have torn me apart. You were in my arms, but I was the one who caused this situation. I have sinned against God, and I will not be able to return.”
verses.36: And my father said to him, “I have smeared your face with oil as an offering to the LORD. Do whatever the LORD has commanded you after he has done what he has done to you. Then you will take revenge on your enemies from among the people of Israel.”
verses.37: And she said to her father, “Let me be freed from this burden. Let me go up to the mountains and stay there alone. My husband and my children will also go with me.”
verses.38: And he said, “Go away.” So he sent her away. She and her sisters went away, and they wandered along the hills.
verses.39: And after two years, she returned to her father. He arranged for her to have a proper marriage. But she knew no one about this arrangement. She remained a widow in Israel.
verses.40: From ancient times onward, the daughters of Israel would go forth to serve the daughter of Jephte. This would take four days each year.
